Delinquency: DPD, SMA and NPA classification

After this lesson you can:
  • Compute DPD and place an account in its bucket
  • Walk the SMA-0/1/2 → NPA ladder and its day-end discipline
  • Explain the financial consequences: income reversal, provisioning, upgrade rules

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

On this page
  1. DPD: the clock that starts at midnight
  2. NPA is a financial event, not a label
  3. The signals a BA should surface
  4. Regulatory anchors
  5. Where this lives in LoanOS
  6. Knowledge check

1. DPD: the clock that starts at midnight

Days Past Due counts from the oldest unpaid due.

Miss an EMI on the 5th, and on the 6th the account is 1 DPD; a partial payment doesn't stop the clock unless it clears the oldest due.

Collections organises accounts into buckets (1–30, 31–60, 61–90, 90+) that drive strategy and staffing.

RBI's stress ladder formalises the early buckets as Special Mention Accounts:

  • SMA-0 — 1–30 days overdue.
  • SMA-1 — 31–60 days.
  • SMA-2 — 61–90 days.

At more than 90 days overdue, the account becomes an NPA.

Classification happens in the day-end process, every day — not at month-end when it looks better.

The IRACP clarifications ended the older habit of month-end-only tagging: an account that crosses 90 DPD on the 17th is an NPA on the 17th.

2. NPA is a financial event, not a label

The moment an account turns NPA:

  1. Income recognition reverses — interest booked but not collected leaves the P&L; future interest accrues only in memorandum (recognised on actual receipt).
  2. Provisioning rises with age and security per IRACP (and Ind AS ECL staging for applicable entities).
  3. Upgrade is strict — the account returns to standard only when *all* arrears of interest and principal are cleared, not when it merely slips under 90 DPD.
  4. Borrower-level pull: for most retail treatment, one NPA loan drags the borrower's other loans with the same RE.

This is why collections intensity concentrates at SMA-2: the 90-day line is where the lender's book, not just the borrower's file, takes the hit.

3. The signals a BA should surface

Good collections analytics measure movement, not just stock: roll rates (share of a bucket that worsens next cycle), cure rates (share that recovers), collection efficiency, and early-warning signals (bounce on first EMI is a famous fraud/quality flag). In LoanOS, delinquency computation and bucket status are ledger-derived — DPD is a function of the event history, so classification is reproducible and reportable (CRILC/SMA reporting feeds off it for applicable exposures).

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-CIR-2025 — Delinquency and default status flow to the CICs in the UCRF cadence; SMA/CRILC reporting for applicable exposures.
  • RBI-DL-2025 — NPA-classification duty is retained by the RE even where a DLG covers losses (see module 8).

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Capability CLL-001 — DPD, overdue amount, bucket and delinquency status.
  • Capability CLL-014 — Collection analytics: roll rates, cure and liquidation.
  • Capability RPT-009 — CRILC/SMA and large-exposure reporting.
  • Code packages/core/src/compliance/compliance-controls.js — Delinquency computation and asset classification on the LMS account model.

Retrieval practice

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. An account is 75 DPD. Its classification?

  1. SMA-0
  2. SMA-1
  3. SMA-2
  4. NPA
Reveal answer and reasoning

C. 61–90 days overdue is SMA-2 — the last stop before NPA at >90 days.

2. An NPA borrower pays enough to reach 45 DPD. Does the account upgrade to standard?

  1. Yes — under 90 now
  2. Yes, after 30 clean days
  3. No — upgrade requires clearing ALL arrears of principal and interest
  4. Only with committee approval
Reveal answer and reasoning

C. IRACP upgrade rules demand full arrear clearance; partial catch-up leaves the account an NPA regardless of the DPD number.
